## I-032 option 2′a: start offsets kept by the Gray code — cost model (before code; gene off by default; predictions/i032-2prime.md, 7ebf20b)

**Gene:** `goff` (0 = today; 1 = the Gray code keeps the start offsets). Off by default, so the reference is unchanged until the user adopts it. Both cores, Python in lockstep.

**What changes, per A** (after the sieved primes' roots r1, r2 and the power entries' roots are computed, in "setup"):
- Each root is converted once to its start offset in sieve coordinates: s0 = r + (M mod p), less p if s0 ≥ p. Power entries use (M mod q).
- This is the same add and conditional subtract the sieve loop performs today per root per polynomial.
- **Charged as `word`, 1 per root** (base roots and power-entry roots), in the setup region (Rust PH_WORD, Python "word").
- `sr` and `qr` then hold offsets instead of x-coordinate roots.

**What changes, per polynomial:**
- **Gray update:** the same arithmetic on the offsets. (s0 ± b) mod p equals ((r ± b) mod p + M mod p) mod p, so the offsets after each switch are identical to what the sieve loop computes today. The charge `setup_gray` × roots is unchanged.
- **Sieve loop:** reads s0 = sr[k] (and qr[t]) directly. **Today's charge "start offsets, one word op per root" (`word` × nr) is not made,** because the add is no longer done. The sieve updates and the width charge are unchanged.
- **Re-sieve** (confirm = resieve): the walk reads s0 directly, so the walk's "+1, the start offset, one word op per root walked" is not made. Every other re-sieve charge is unchanged.
- **Root pass** (confirm = root): reads s0 directly in place of recomputing it. Its store charge (`word` × sr.len) is unchanged; removing that pass is 2′b, not built here.
- **Python traces:** keep recording x-coordinate roots `(p, r)` in `at["polys"][...]["roots"]` (qs_accept, parity, sieveshare and startoff_accept read them). In goff mode the trace recovers r = s0 − (M mod p) mod p **for the trace only**. That is trace bookkeeping, not card work, and is not charged, as the trace's other fields are not.

**Expected counts at 96** (from the I-032 model's measured inputs, f12ae23; reference genes + goff):
- `word` −263.8 × 156.04 + 263.8 × 19.955 ≈ **−35,900 per number**. Every other type is unchanged.
- Official, ruint and Montgomery totals are not computed or compared here (predictions/i032-2prime.md, R2-1/R2-2, D-1/D-2). Acceptance compares counts by type and identity only.

**Identity:**
- Same offsets, so the same sieve array, the same candidates, the same divisions, relations and factor.
- **Acceptance** (`evolve/goff_accept.py`), all map numbers 54–96, for the new reference, + re-sieve, + root, + pp 3 and + pp 10:
  1. goff off against the pre-change binary: identical per number and per type.
  2. goff on against goff off: identical factor, candidates, hits, polynomials (sieve_scan), sieve_update and every type except `word`. The `word` difference equals −(roots per polynomial × polynomials) + (roots per A × A's), plus, under re-sieve, −(roots walked).
  3. Relations (u, sparse vector, y) and every candidate value identical, from Python traces, 2 numbers per size.
  4. Python = Rust per type, on and off.
- **Parity:** goff cases added.

**Not an uncharged op:** the per-A conversion is charged. The removed charges correspond to work that is no longer done.

**Code:** per the cost model (30d3ead), in both cores, with gene `goff` (off by default).

## Results policy for other machines (friend runs and contributors' timings; documentation only)

- **Friend runs are replications labelled by machine** (host, CPU, cores, OS, pinned or not). They are made with the kit (`tools/friend_setup.sh`, `tools/friend_run.sh <run-name>` from a committed `runs/<run-name>.json`, `evolve/friend_timing.py`).
- **Ratios are compared within a machine.** They are never pooled across machines without saying so.
- **A friend run is scored only against predictions sealed for that run.** Otherwise it is information.
- **The user commits the returned file.** Claude Code neither requests nor uploads results files.
- **Contributors' `tools/contribute_timing.sh` results are information only.**
- Rules in PROTOCOL.md, "Replications on other machines".

## I-032 option 2′b: root confirm reads the kept offsets in place — cost model (before code; `wolfram/2026-10-27_i032b_cost.wl`, `.out`; predictions/i032-2prime.md)

**Scope:**
- **No new gene.** When goff = 1 and confirm = root, root confirm's per-polynomial pass (qs.rs:945–967; qs.py's per-polynomial `rtab`) is removed. The root test reads the offsets the Gray code keeps (`sr`, Python `st_`) through a per-A index.
- With goff = 0, root confirm is unchanged, so root-confirm and root-confirm-2 stay reproducible.
- The runner's 2′b cells (`goff=1, confirm="root"`, evolve/i032time.py, 3f4034e) take the new path.

**Per A** (in "setup", after 2′a's conversion), for the sieved odd primes of that A (132.2 per A at 96 bits):
- `ka[t]`, the index in `sr` of prime t's first root, and `tm[t]`, its reciprocal (copied from the per-attempt `recip`).
- **Charged `word` × 2 per sieved prime.**
- Prime t's last root is `ka[t + 1] − 1`, or `sr.len() − 1` for the last prime: a compare, no stored sentinel, so no extra charge. A single-root prime (p | k) has first = last.
- p and the base index are read as `sp[ka[t]]` and `sj[ka[t]]` (reads; no copy, no charge).
- Python keeps per A a list of (base index, the prime's entry in `st_`). Its offsets are read live, since the Gray code rebinds them. Its charge is the same, 2 per sieved prime.
- A's primes (`aj`) are formed per A instead of per polynomial. That is uncharged as today: it is a sort of s indices that today's code also does without a charge, and it moves without change.

**Per polynomial:** the root pass and its charge (`word` × sieved roots, 263.8 per polynomial) are gone. Nothing replaces them.

**Per candidate:** unchanged.
- root_test × sieved primes.
- The low-bit test (1 word), A's primes by v mod p (confirm_td each), the first division by each hit and an even v (confirm_td), and the merged list (`word` × |plist|).
- **No negative-x handling:** the offsets are in sieve coordinates and i0 ≥ 0.
- The reciprocal reduction is the same arithmetic, on `sr[ka[t]]` / `sr[last]` in place of `ta[t]` / `tb[t]`. Same hits, same order (ascending base index).

**Exact structure** (Python traces of the reference genes, all 640 map numbers at 96 bits; polynomials 156.042 and setup_gray 35,897.39 agree exactly with lampcore):
- 19.955 A's (7.82 polynomials per A);
- 2,638.08 sieved primes summed over A's;
- 41,162.74 sieved roots summed over polynomials (the pass);
- 5,265.36 summed over A's (2′a's conversion);
- root mode's per-candidate words 8,058.6 per number (7.96 per candidate).

**Expected counts, 2′b against 2′a** (means per number):
- `word` +8,058.6 (per candidate) + 5,276.2 (ka, tm);
- root_test +135,730.6;
- confirm_td −129,701.3;
- setup_small +137.8 (the per-attempt reciprocals, as in today's root mode).
- Every other type is identical.
- **Against today's root mode (goff off):** `word` −41,162.7 (the pass) − 35,897.4 (2′a) + 5,276.2 (ka, tm).

**Model** (the Wolfram run above; model, not a verdict; the sealed predictions stay as written):
- 2′a / REF 0.9754 / 0.9843 / 0.9842 (official / ruint / Montgomery);
- **2′b / 2′a 1.0137 / 0.8877 / 0.8838**, unchanged to 4 digits from f12ae23's estimate. The exact per-A build (2 × 132.2 per A) is 72 word per number below f12ae23's 2 × 134.0 × 19.955.
- For information: 2′b / REF 0.9888 / 0.8738 / 0.8698, and 2′b / today's root 0.9527 / 0.9654 / 0.9650.
- These are counts × prices from the REF and today's-root counts already used in f12ae23, plus trace structure. They are not measured 2′b or 2′a totals.

**What the model does not establish:**
- any wall-clock;
- that the code matches the note. Acceptance checks that: the counts above to the op, per number.

**Acceptance** (`evolve/rootb_accept.py`), all map numbers 54–96; genomes the new reference, + pp 3, + pp 10, the corrected reference:
1. goff = 0 and confirm = root against the pre-change binary (a6d67a2): identical per number and per type.
2. 2′b (goff = 1, root) against 2′a (goff = 1, full pass): the same factor, candidates, hits and polynomials. Types change only as follows:
   - root_test, confirm_td and setup_small equal today's root mode against the full pass (goff off), per number;
   - `word` 2′b − 2′a equals today's (root − full) word, less the pass (word × sieved roots per polynomial), plus 2 × sieved primes per A.

4. Python = Rust per type for 2′b, 2′a and goff off + root.

**Parity:** goff + root cases already run (a6d67a2's parity added `qs goff root`). Low caps inside the per-A build and the root test are added.

## pp 3 on 2′b: the meter against wall-clock (post hoc, read-only; `wolfram/2026-10-27_pp3_gap.wl`, `.out`; no new timing; no meter change)

**Question:** 2′b+pp3 against 2′b is −5.1% official (−2.0% ruint, −2.1% Montgomery), but wall-clock is +2.0% (3,475.3 against 3,407.9 µs at 2.4 GHz, i032-2prime, 9b94247). Where does wall-clock rise while price falls or holds?

**Inputs:**
- **Wall-clock:** the sealed run's `i032time.json`. **Only wall, sieve and confirm were saved per cell;** setup, gray, scan, lp_ledger and solve are one remainder ("rest").
- **Priced per region (ruint):** lampcore `--phasetime`'s per-region type counts, counts only, with the ns discarded.
- **Instrumentation bug, found here:** `pt_end` (`lampcore/src/main.rs`) copies type columns `0..29` only, so **root_test (column 29) is attributed to no region** in `--phasetime`'s per-region types.
  - The meter, `--types` and the region ns are unaffected.
  - Here root_test is added to confirm by hand (all of it is charged there). With that, the regions sum to the total within 3.5 ruint.
  - Not fixed (a lampcore change; the user's call).

| region | wall 2′b → 2′b+pp3 (µs) | ruint 2′b → 2′b+pp3 | µs per ruint (2′b, pp3) | wall change if it tracked price | wall above price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sieve | 968.6 → 906.5 (−6.4%) | 23,455 → 21,152 (−9.8%) | 0.0413, 0.0429 | −95.1 | **+33.0 µs** |
| confirm (incl. root_test) | 606.3 → 732.0 (+20.7%) | 9,583 → 11,654 (+21.6%) | 0.0633, 0.0628 | +131.0 | −5.3 µs |
| rest (setup, gray, scan, lp_ledger, solve, mult, fb) | 1,833.0 → 1,836.8 (+0.2%) | 18,573 → 17,792 (−4.2%) | 0.0987, 0.1032 | −77.1 | **+80.9 µs** |
| total | +2.0% | −2.0% | | | +108.6 µs |

**Readings:**
- **Confirm tracks its price** (+20.7% wall against +21.6% ruint). It is where pp 3's +21% candidates cost time (1,012.7 → 1,227.4 per number), at the same 0.60 µs per candidate.
- **Sieve:** price per polynomial is flat (150.3 → 150.6 ruint), but wall per polynomial rises 4.0% (6.21 → 6.45 µs).
  - pp 3's work per polynomial costs more time than its price. The free-2 initialisation (a stride-2 write over half the interval, charged under the width charge, NOTES "Stage H") and the power-entry walks are priced as ordinary sieve work.
  - About +33 µs per number.
- **Rest: the largest gap** (+81 µs). Its price falls 4.2%: fewer A's (20.95 → 19.0 setup entries) and polynomials (156.0 → 140.5) cut setup and gray. Its wall-clock holds.
  - The run did not save the sub-regions, so how much setup and gray fell, against how much lp_ledger rose, is not measured.
  - lp_ledger's price rises 19.5% (1,920 → 2,294 ruint): partials looked up +22.4% (916 → 1,121), kept-relation copies +19.9% (994 → 1,192), combinations 71.9 → 78.6.
- **The hypothesis (the large-prime table's hash at 1.4–1.7× its price, open question 4) explains little:** the hash type rises by +402.7 ops (146.5 ruint), so an excess of 0.4–0.7× is 59–103 ruint, **~4–7 µs** of the ~81 µs.
  - Step 3 measured the kept-relation copy at ~100 ns per call for ~25 ns priced (the heap allocation of each sparse list). +198 copies would then be ~15–30 µs unpriced, clock-dependent.
  - **So the large-prime table is a candidate for part of the rest gap, mainly through copies rather than the hash.** That is not established: the ns figures come from earlier runs at an unknown clock, and this run has no lp_ledger wall-clock.
- **Official's −5.1% is mostly the sieve:** sieve_update −73,497 and sieve_scan −32,926 ops per number (−7.4 points of official), against root_test +28,712 and word +7,302. Official prices a sieve update the same as a root test, and that is where official and wall-clock part most.

**What would settle it** (not run): one capped timed run of 2′b and 2′b+pp3 saving every region per replicate, plus a `LAMPCORE_LPBREAK=1` pass for lp:copy, lp:hash and lp:comb ns. The shift-test runner (below) saves all regions.

**Model, post hoc, not a verdict.**

## Decision (the user's, Oct 26): goff = 1 adopted as the reference default

- **The reference genes change only by goff = 1** (I-032 option 2′a). Relations, factors, candidates and polynomials are identical (a6d67a2 acceptance; i032-2prime identity 640 / 640), so **earlier results stay valid.** Only the word count differs, by exactly −setup_gray per number.
- **The shift test's base (2′a) is now the reference.**
- **reviews/card_params.md updated.**
- **Code:** runners pass `goff=1` explicitly. The reference helper `lctest.ref()` and the sealed genes file still return goff absent, so the scripts of earlier runs reproduce exactly as committed. Making goff = 1 the code default of `ref()` would change what earlier scripts compute on a rerun, so it is left as is. It can be done as a separate commit if the user wants.

### For the record, unscored (the phase predictions are information only; breakdown seen first)

- **D-11:** its falsifier would trigger. The whole "rest" (lp_ledger included) totals ~81 µs above price, under D-11's 120 µs floor for lp_ledger.
- **R2-11:** its first half (mostly outside the sieve) would hold, since the sieve shows +33 µs and the rest +81 µs. Its ledger claim would fail: the hash explains 4–7 µs at most, and lp_ledger's share is not measured.
- **The reviewer's correction (recorded as given):** the "241 µs / 7-point gap" given to the outside reviewers took official's ratio as the priced expectation. Official prices a sieve update like a root test, so most of official's −5.1% is sieve savings. Against ruint the gap is about 4 points, 109 µs. **This error was the reviewer's.**

### lampcore `--phasetime` instrumentation fix (tooling only; the meter and `--types` unchanged)

- **(1) root_test now counted in its region.** `pt_end` copied type columns `0..29` only, so root_test (column 29, added with root confirm, e13603a) was attributed to no region. It now loops `0..N_TY`.
- **(2) lp_ledger region closed on all exits.** The region was not closed on three early returns: the ledger full after a direct add, the ledger full after a combination, and a factor found as a large prime. The last relation's ops and ns per attempt fell outside every region (~3.5 ruint per number at 96). It is now closed on those paths.
- **Checks:**
  - Per-region type counts sum exactly to the `--types` totals on every map number at 96 (640) and 72 (480) bits, for REF, 2′a, 2′b and 2′b+pp3.
  - `--types` and every result are identical to the pre-fix binary on all map numbers 54–96, for 7 genomes (14,000 / 14,000).
  - Parity passes: qs 5,214 and types 7,986 pairs, mismatches 0; mutations 56 / 56. Output in `parity_ptfix.out`.
- **Python** has no `--phasetime` equivalent, so it is unaffected.
- **Effect on earlier results:** none on counts or priced totals. Earlier per-region priced figures from `--phasetime` lacked root_test in confirm (the pp 3 breakdown, 8d5ef90, added it by hand) and lacked the ~3.5 ruint residue. Region ns are unchanged except that lp_ledger now includes the last relation's time (one per attempt).

### DeepSeek's view (received 00:32 Oct 27 PT; information only; verbatim)

<!-- verbatim begin -->
## My view on the robust rule

The robust rule is doing exactly what it was designed to do: it is a pre-committed safeguard against overfitting to any single measure, and the fact that it vetoes a result the clock likes is evidence it is working, not a bug. The strongest argument for keeping it is that changing the rule after seeing an inconvenient result is the classic path to overfitting; the disagreement between official and wall-clock is real information, and it says the cost models are not yet good enough to settle sieve-versus-confirm trades, which is precisely when the conservative rule should bind. If official is genuinely wrong for this trade—and tonight's 0.9807 and 1.0138 suggest it is—the right fix is to **re-price official's sieve update prospectively and restate the rule prospectively**, not to drop official because a sealed result came out inconvenient. RAPL energy is the right long-term arbiter, but until it is readable the minimax rule should stand; if the user does revisit it, the decision should be committed before the next test and applied to all cells, including the ones that already favour the current rule.

No sealed prediction is revised. D-13 and D-14 are recorded as falsified; D-12 held; the official-climbs-faster miss is shared across all three tables and noted. The shift run and the running A/B runs are noted as unscored for me; anything I send now is information only.
<!-- verbatim end -->

**The reviewer's note:** the shift results show that official disagrees with wall-clock on this machine, not that it is wrong. Whether a hardware-neutral count should hold a veto is a design choice, not a measurement.

Re-price official's sieve update going forward so that it tracks the measured wall cost of a sieve step rather than equating it to a root test. ### DeepSeek's second view (received 00:45 Oct 27 PT; information only; verbatim)

<!-- verbatim begin -->
## 1. Does my view change?

Partly. The reviewer's point is correct: re-pricing official's sieve update to track wall-clock would make official a second machine-calibrated pricing, and ruint already serves that role; the robust track would then have no hardware-neutral member, and its "worst of three" would be worst of three machine-specific estimates. That is a real loss. But the point cuts both ways: an official pricing that is wrong about which ops matter is not guarding against anything useful—it is vetoing results on a mis-specified cost, which is what happened at +2 (official 1.0138 while wall was −12.0%, best). The cleanest fix is therefore not to mutate official and not to drop it, but to **add a fourth, prospective pricing** that keeps official's op-counting spirit while counting a sieve update as a fraction of a root test, and to decide the robust rule (worst-of-three vs worst-of-four, or a documented exception process) **before** the next test. That preserves a hardware-neutral member, fixes the known mis-specification, and avoids the appearance of rescuing tonight's result. My substantive view is unchanged: keep the rule, fix the pricing prospectively, do not change it after seeing an inconvenient cell.

## 2. Is adopting pp3 overfitting to the meter?

Yes, substantially. Against 2'b directly, pp3 is +0.7% wall at +1 and −0.9% at +2/+3—within cross-run drift of ±1.5 points—and its only clear benefit is pulling official below 1.0 at 96, the very pricing the reviewer argues is mis-specified. Adopting a component whose measured effect is to satisfy one known-questionable pricing, while neutral on wall-clock, is optimizing for the meter rather than for the machine; the honest adoption candidate on wall-clock grounds is **2'b alone** (−11.2%), with pp3 treated as a 96-bit workaround for the official pricing quirk until the pricing is fixed prospectively.
<!-- verbatim end -->

### Grok's second view (received 00:47 Oct 27 PT; information only; verbatim)

<!-- verbatim begin -->
**Information-only views**

1. The fourth pricing is legitimate if the fraction is fixed from a public, machine-independent instruction taxonomy written before the test and applied uniformly; it becomes rescue-by-redefinition if the fraction is chosen so that 2'b clears the new robust threshold on these particular numbers. Official already treats every counted operation as unit cost; introducing a pre-declared relative weight between two op classes preserves that spirit while removing an arbitrary equality the phase data have shown to be false. The strongest safeguard is that the fraction must be published and frozen before any of the 72/84/96-bit 2'b runs begin, and that the same fraction is then used for every future cell, not re-tuned after the results appear.

2. Count the retired micro-operations (or, on a non-Intel target, the corresponding ISA-level memory and arithmetic instructions) required by a representative sieve-update sequence versus a representative root-test sequence, using only the documented instruction semantics and a single fixed compiler/ISA model; the ratio of those two counts becomes the fraction. Because the counts come from the instruction definitions rather than from timed runs on any particular CPU, the fraction remains hardware-neutral and can be re-derived by anyone from the same source descriptions.

3. Yes: pp3 is neutral-to-slightly-negative on wall-clock against 2'b at 96 bits and fails the existing robust rule at every size tested, so adopting it now would be fitting the pipeline to the current official pricing rather than to measured work.

**The reviewer's notes:**
- **Q2:** "retired micro-operations" vary by microarchitecture. The hardware-neutral version counts ISA-level instructions in one fixed compiled sequence per op class.
  - Op counts ignore memory cost, and a sieve update is mostly memory. That is acceptable for an op-count pricing, but it must be stated.
- **Q3 misstates the result:** at 96, pp 3 +1 passed the robust rule (robust 0.9807, better). The conclusion (adopting pp 3 now would fit the meter) stands.
- **A "sealed test" of a new pricing tests nothing:** priced outcomes are deterministic from counts already measured. The safeguard must be on the fraction's derivation.
- **Order if option (2) is chosen:**
  1. Commit the derivation procedure.
  2. Compute the fraction mechanically and commit it.
  3. Only then compute and publish the break-even fraction for 2′b and 2′b's ratio.

### Requirements for the op-class procedure (DeepSeek, received 05:18 Oct 27 PT; information only; verbatim)

<!-- verbatim begin -->
## 1. Requirements the op-class procedure draft must meet

- **Op classes from a public ISA-level taxonomy, not from timing.** The classes (e.g. integer multiply, load, store, compare/branch, reciprocal-style multiply-shift) must be enumerated from the instruction-set description, with the compiler/ISA model and flags named. Any micro-op cross-check is secondary, published with a stated tolerance, and used to flag divergence, not to replace the ISA-level ratio.
- **Representative sequences chosen and frozen before any 2'b run at any size.** The sieve-update sequence and the root-test sequence should be the card's own kernels, named by commit, with the exact instruction stream or a re-derivable recipe. Two independent readers with the same source description and the same frozen choices must get the same ratio; if they don't, the choices were underspecified.
- **Mechanical computation, committed, then published.** Procedure first, fraction second, break-even fraction and 2'b's ratio only after the fraction is committed. No re-tuning afterwards; version-named (e.g. `official_v2_sieve_fraction=…`) so any later revision is visibly a new version.
- **Sub-op counts published, not just the scalar.** The ratio alone hides which sub-op is being re-weighted; the counts let a reader re-derive it and see whether the re-weighting is dominated by one class.
- **The decision rule fixed before the break-even is published.** Worst-of-four, or an explicit exception process, must be chosen before anyone sees whether 2'b clears it. And the fraction must not be derived from wall-clock; otherwise official becomes a second machine-calibrated pricing and the hardware-neutral member of the robust track is lost.

## 2. My most common error type, and one rule to add

My most common error is **transferring an effect across operating points without a mechanism-derived scaling**: carrying the 96-bit pp3 effect to 72/84 (D-15 priced, above both results), and centering sealed ranges on a single model output rather than on the arithmetic's own band (D-8 ruint sealed 0.975–0.990 after computing 0.959–0.978). A close second is **misreading which comparison a single quoted number describes** — the "robust 0.982" was worst-of-three against today's reference, not the marginal pp3 effect I treated it as — and a third is **definition ambiguity in the prediction itself** (D-17's "largest difference" versus "largest increase").

Rule to add: **every sealed range must be derived from an explicit arithmetic band, and any cross-size or cross-cell transfer must name the scaling assumption and widen the range by the measured cross-run drift (±1.5 points) plus a stated size-transfer allowance; before using a single quoted number, state which comparison, which base, and which pricing it refers to.** That rule would have caught D-15 priced, D-8 ruint, and the D-17 definition ambiguity at seal time rather than at scoring.
<!-- verbatim end -->

**The reviewer's notes:**
- **"Frozen before any 2′b run" is already past** (2b-sizes, 5d8e1c9, timed 2′b at 72 and 84). The operative requirement: the procedure and the fraction are frozen **before 2′b's ratio under the new pricing is computed or seen**. Priced outcomes are deterministic from existing counts, so that is the point the freeze protects.
- **Added requirement (the reviewer): scope.** The op-class weighting covers **every op class official prices at unit cost**, not only sieve updates and root tests.

**Use:** this list (DeepSeek's requirements, with the two notes above) is the checklist when the draft (`reviews/opclass_procedure_DRAFT.md`) is reviewed. Not yet applied to the draft; the draft is unchanged.

### Requirement 6 (the reviewer, answering Grok): no hand-picked sequences

- **Each op class's weight = retired instructions per op**, measured over a whole run of the frozen binary. The compiler, its version and its flags are named and frozen first.
- **Attributed to op types across all call sites:** for example an instructions-retired counter per op region, or static instruction counts of every site weighted by its execution count.

- **State with every figure:** retired-instruction counts are fixed by the binary, not by clock speed; memory cost is excluded.

## Sieve breakdown and clock samples in short cells (tooling only; no charge changes; no timed run)

### Sieve breakdown (lampcore `--phasetime`, `LAMPCORE_SIEVEBREAK=1`)

- **Five sub-regions inside the sieve region,** timed only with `LAMPCORE_SIEVEBREAK=1` (like `LAMPCORE_LPBREAK=1` for lp_ledger):
  - `sv:zero`: the array cleared;
  - `sv:free2`: pp's free-2 initialisation (stage H; one stride-2 write over half the interval);
  - `sv:prime`: the base-prime walks (ordinary updates);
  - `sv:power`: the power-entry walks (pp);
  - `sv:tail`: the charges, the root pass (root confirm without goff) and the scan event.
- **Op units per sub-region.** The sieve region charges its updates once, at its end, so the meter's per-region types cannot split them. Each sub-region therefore gets "units": the sieve_update, sieve_scan and word ops it would carry (zero: the width charge; prime and power: updates plus start-offset words; tail: the root pass's words; free2: none, since it is under the width charge). The units are counted only with the flag on and are never charged.
- **pp 3 has no power entries at 54–96 bits:** powers must be below 2³ = 8, which admits no odd prime power (9 > 8) and no 2^j with j ≥ 4. **pp 3's only sieve work is the free-2 initialisation** (and the second threshold at the scan). `sv:power` is exercised by pp 10 in the acceptance.
- **Acceptance** (`evolve/svbreak_accept.py`, `svbreak_accept.out`; 7 genomes: the reference, + goff, + goff + root, + goff + root + pp 3, + pp 10, + root + pp 10, + goff + pp 10):
  1. `--types` and every result identical to the pre-change binary on all map numbers 54–96: **14,000 / 14,000**.
  2. With the flag on (every 8th map number): units sum to the sieve region's sieve_update + sieve_scan + word; the four walk sub-regions carry no types; the top-level regions' types sum to the `--types` totals: **1,750 / 1,750**.
  3. With the flag off: the sub-regions have no calls, ns or units; the regions sum to the totals: **1,750 / 1,750**.
- **Parity:** passes (`evolve/parity_svbreak.out`): qs 5,214 and types 7,986 pairs, mismatches 0, sum-identity failures 0; race 653, ob 369, guards 54; mutations caught 56 / 56.
- **Overhead:** with the flag on, the sieve region's ns rises (~5 snaps per polynomial). Sub-region ns are therefore information, like the lp: ones; a timed run that uses them should time the wall-clock replicates with the flag off and run one breakdown pass per cell, as with LPBREAK.
- **Smoke observation (information only; 10 numbers at 96, one pass, sub-timers on, not a timed run):** `sv:free2` took ~40 µs per number in 2′b+pp3 with zero units. That is the size of the sieve excess against 2′b in run A (+58 to +69 µs), but nothing is established until a timed run measures it.
- **Python** has no `--phasetime`, so it is unaffected. `lctest.phasetime(g, nums, lpb, svb=False)` passes the flag and returns each sub-region's units.

### Clock samples in short cells (`evolve/timing.py`)

- **The problem (be7579b):** the sampler read core 2's MHz at each cell's launch and then every 1 s. A 72-bit cell takes ~0.35 s, so each had one sample, read before the core ramped. The flags at 72 rested on that.
- **New options, opt-in** (the defaults are unchanged, so earlier runners reproduce as committed):
  - `period`: seconds between samples (0.05 for short cells);
  - `skip_launch`: the first sample is read after one period, not at launch;
  - `inner`: each cell timed `inner` times back to back per replicate, ns averaged (`mean_passes`);
  - `svb`: the sieve sub-regions timed;
  - every cell's clock summary now also gives `per_pass` (samples per timed pass) and `valid` (`per_pass` ≥ 3). A flag on a cell that is not valid rests on too few samples.
- **Check (2 replicates, 72 bits, 2′a and 2′b+pp3; information):**
  - Defaults: 1 sample per pass; medians 400 and 1,460 MHz; one cell flagged; neither valid.
  - `period=0.05, skip_launch=True`: 11 samples per pass; **both medians 2,400 MHz; no flag; both valid.**
  - The same with `inner=3`: 10–11 per pass; 2,400 MHz.
  - So the 72-bit flags in shift-72-84 most likely came from the launch sample. This check is not a re-run of those cells.

**Not done:** no timed run (as briefed). No charge, count or price changed.

## Meter correction (proposed; cost note only, before any code; the user decides): pp's free-2 initialisation is uncharged

**Label: a meter correction** (an op the meter does not count), separate from re-pricing (the open decision on official's prices). CLAUDE.md: "An uncharged op is a critical bug."

**The op:**
- With pp > 0, every polynomial's sieve starts by writing the prime 2's fixed log w2 into every second cell of the interval: `for x in arr[par..].iter_mut().step_by(2) { *x = w2; }` (`lampcore/src/qs.rs`, stage H). Python does the same.
- **It is not charged.** The comment says "under the width charge", but the width charge (one sieve_scan per cell) already pays for clearing the array and for the scan. The free-2 writes are extra work, about width / 2 byte stores per polynomial.
- **Without pp, the prime 2 is not sieved at all** (the base walks start at j = 2), so this is new work that pp adds, not work moved from elsewhere.
- **pp 3 has no power entries at 54–96 bits** (NOTES, "Sieve breakdown"), so this write is pp 3's only sieve work.

**Proposed charge:**
- **Count:** one op per cell written, ⌈(width − par) / 2⌉ per polynomial. width = 2M + 1 is odd and par ∈ {0, 1}, so per number this is sieve_scan / 2 within ± polynomials / 2 (at most 0.0002 relative at 96).
- **Type: sieve_scan** (proposed). The op class is one byte store per cell in a regular stride-2 pass, like the array clear and the scan that the width charge already types as sieve_scan. It is not a sieve update, which is a read-modify-write at a prime stride.
  - **Alternative, sieve_update:** a strided store. Computed below for sensitivity.
  - The type is chosen by op class, not from wall-clock. For reference only, the smoke breakdown measured ~0.27 ns per write at 96; that figure was not used.
- **Python and Rust** would charge it identically (parity), in the sieve phase.

**What the priced ratios would become** (`wolfram/2026-10-27_free2_charge.wl`, `.out`; counts from lampcore `--types`, card d269cc8, means over all map numbers; 2′a and 2′b have no pp and are unchanged; model, not a verdict):

| cell | free-2 writes / number | as now (official / ruint / Montgomery) | charged as sieve_scan | robust now → charged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 72 +0 vs 2′a | 11,917 | 1.0289 / 0.9043 / 0.8971 | 1.1085 / 0.9212 / 0.9149 | 1.0289 → 1.1085 |
| 72 +1 | 12,761 | 1.0171 / 0.8779 / 0.8698 | 1.1023 / 0.8959 / 0.8889 | 1.0171 → 1.1023 |
| 72 +2 | 13,722 | 1.0186 / 0.8590 / 0.8533 | 1.1102 / 0.8784 / 0.8739 | 1.0186 → 1.1102 |
| 84 +0 | 42,507 | 1.0020 / 0.8805 / 0.8740 | 1.0955 / 0.9040 / 0.8985 | 1.0020 → 1.0955 |
| 84 +1 | 44,845 | 0.9987 / 0.8567 / 0.8505 | 1.0973 / 0.8815 / 0.8764 | 0.9987 → 1.0973 |
| 84 +2 | 47,807 | 1.0108 / 0.8488 / 0.8412 | 1.1160 / 0.8753 / 0.8687 | 1.0108 → 1.1160 |
| 96 +0 | 148,459 | 0.9618 / 0.8703 / 0.8656 | 1.0659 / 0.9018 / 0.8981 | 0.9618 → 1.0659 |
| 96 +1 | 157,401 | 0.9807 / 0.8671 / 0.8620 | 1.0911 / 0.9005 / 0.8965 | 0.9807 → 1.0911 |
| 96 +2 | 168,480 | 1.0138 / 0.8748 / 0.8710 | 1.1320 / 0.9106 / 0.9079 | 1.0138 → 1.1320 |
| 96 +3 | 181,593 | 1.0595 / 0.8943 / 0.8913 | 1.1869 / 0.9329 / 0.9310 | 1.0595 → 1.1869 |

- **Against 2′b at 96:**
  - +0: now 0.9488 / 0.9804 / 0.9794; charged as sieve_scan **1.0515 / 1.0159 / 1.0162**.
  - +1: now 0.9674 / 0.9768 / 0.9754; charged **1.0764 / 1.0145 / 1.0144**.
- **As sieve_update** (alternative), ruint and Montgomery rise further. For example, 96 +0 against 2′a would be 1.0659 / 0.9361 / 0.9319, and against 2′b 1.0515 / 1.0546 / 1.0544.

**Reading (model):**
- **pp 3's official saving is the uncharged write.** The free-2 writes are 7.7–12.0% of official per number. Charged, every 2′b+pp3 cell is worse than 2′a under official at every size (1.07–1.19), and **2′b+pp3 at 96 is worse than 2′b under all three pricings** at +0 and +1.
- **Every robust "better" call for 2′b+pp3** (i032-2prime; pp3-gap-and-shift +0 and +1; shift-past-2 +1) **rests on this uncharged op.** Those results stand as recorded under the meter of their day; this note does not rescore them.
- ruint and Montgomery still show 2′b+pp3 below 2′a (0.88–0.93 as sieve_scan), because root confirm's saving is much larger than the write's cost. Against 2′b they show pp 3 a little worse (~+1.5%), consistent with wall-clock (+0.7% at +1, −0.9% at +2, run A).
- This is consistent with the sieve excess pp 3 showed against 2′b in run A (+58 to +69 µs) and the ~40 µs `sv:free2` smoke figure. R2-20 (2b-sizes) measures that directly.

**Was the width charge calibrated to include initialisation writes?** (DeepSeek's point, 01:39 Oct 27: if it was, split the width charge into clearing and free-2 initialisation instead of adding a second charge, to avoid double-counting.) Checked against the record:
- **The width charge's count is width per polynomial, the same with pp on or off.** The audit (NOTES, item on re-sieve initialisation) recorded the sieve array's re-zeroing as covered by it, together with the scan: one sieve_scan per cell, for both passes.
- **sieve_scan's price comes from the Oct 23 opbench microbenchmark** (52e4e53, "2026-10-23 — Op-price calibration"). That was three days before the free-2 write existed: stage H first added the free 2 as a parity-dependent threshold at the scan, with no per-position work, and the scan fix (cad255f, Oct 26) turned it into a stride-2 write with "charges: none change", so that the counts stayed identical to the threshold version.
- **So neither the count nor the price of the width charge includes the free-2 writes.** Adding a separate charge (⌈(width − par) / 2⌉ per polynomial) does not double-count; splitting the width charge would leave the writes uncounted. **The proposal stays an added charge.**
- The scan fix's equivalence argument concerned candidates, not cost. Under the threshold design the per-position cost was a parity selection inside the scan's existing compare; under the write design it is a half pass of stores.

**Not done:** no code changed; nothing rescored. Applying the correction (code, parity, and stating which earlier results it would affect) is the user's decision.

## Free-2 meter correction: applied (the user's decision, APPLY after the 2b-sizes run; code, acceptance, parity)

- **The charge:** with pp on, each polynomial charges `sieve` with ⌈(width − par) / 2⌉, the cells the free-2 initialisation writes, typed **sieve_scan**.
  - Rust adds the count to the scan event (`EV_SIEVE_SCAN`, beside the width) and to the sieve breakdown's `sv:free2` units.
  - Python adds it to the trace's per-polynomial "f2", which `optypes.qs_counts` adds to sieve_scan.
  - The charge comes right after the width charge in both twins. In Rust the event is recorded with the width's, after the root pass, so a run that hits its budget mid-polynomial types the same in both.
- **Unchanged:** every genome without pp (the reference, 2′a, 2′b, root confirm), and every count, factor, test and hit with pp except sieve_scan and total ops.
- **Acceptance** (`evolve/free2_accept.py`, `free2_accept.out`; all map numbers 54–96, against the pre-change binary):
  1. Without pp (4 genomes): identical per number and per type, **8,000 / 8,000**.
  2. With pp (6 genomes: pp 3 with goff + root at +0 and +2 bits, pp 3, pp 10, root + pp 10, goff + pp 10): only sieve_scan and total ops change, by the same positive amount, **12,000 / 12,000**.
  3. With pp, 2 numbers per size per genome: the increase equals the cells written, counted independently as `len(range(par, 2M + 1, 2))` over the traced polynomials; Python = Rust per type and in ops: **48 / 48**.
  - Sieve breakdown units still equal the sieve region's sieve_update + sieve_scan + word (84 / 84; 72 and 96 bits, 3 genomes).
- **Parity passes** (`evolve/parity_free2.out`): qs 5,214 and types 7,986 pairs, mismatches 0, sum-identity failures 0; race 653, ob 369, guards 54; mutations 56 / 56.
- **From this commit on, every priced figure of a pp cell is under the corrected meter.** Earlier results keep their scores. The affected outcomes (the "meter-invalidated" table above) get a second score under the corrected meter, side by side, by the adopted rule. **The second scores are not yet computed.**

### 1. Audit item 17: A mod p per base prime per A is uncharged (both cores)

- **Facts** (NOTES, "Audit item 17", fix C.1): for each base prime and each A, Rust computes `a % p` to skip A's own primes, then again as the Euclid input; Python computes `A % p` in the `sieved` list and in `euclid_inv`. The Euclid charge counts only its division steps; the reduction itself is uncharged.
- **Proposed charge:** one setup_small op per base prime per A, A × (F − 2) per number, typed setup_small (a small-modulus reduction), matching how the power entries' A mod q is already charged (stage H).
  - The second Rust reduction is the same value. **Proposed code alongside:** reduce once and reuse, so the charge stays one per prime.
- **Expected size** (A × (F − 2) per number: 386 / 1,001 / 2,707 at 72 / 84 / 96):

  | size | official | ruint | Montgomery |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 72 | +0.26% | +1.35% | +1.41% |
  | 84 | +0.22% | +1.37% | +1.41% |
  | 96 | +0.19% | +1.43% | +1.45% |

  - Twice that if both Rust reductions were charged. The earlier ~1.9% estimate assumed ~27 A's per number; the current reference uses 19.9 at 96.
- **Effect on comparisons:** it scales with A's, which 2′a, 2′b and root confirm share. It shifts every cell's total about equally, so ratios between relation-identical cells barely move.

### 2. The large-prime table's hash

- **Facts:** step 3 measured the like-for-like op mix at 1.4–1.7× the calibrated hash price at every size.
  - **Tonight's LPBREAK data** (sub-timers on, so an upper bound) give lp:hash at **1.48× (72), 1.77× (84), 2.61× (96)** of its price at each cell's mean µs per ruint: 91 / 90 / 120 ns per lookup against 61 / 51 / 46 ns priced.
- **Expected size:**
  - at 1.4–1.7×, the unpriced part is 0.95–1.66% (72), 0.60–1.05% (84), 0.48–0.84% (96) of ruint;
  - at the measured ratio it is 7.9 / 16.8 / 67.8 µs, i.e. 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.8% of wall.
- **Proposed measurement first:** the meter-health check's (a) on lp:hash with the sub-timers' own overhead measured, then a microbenchmark of the card's table (insert and lookup at the card's sizes), before any re-price. This is a price question, not a missing charge.

### 3. Kept-relation copies

- **Facts:** each kept relation's sparse list is copied into the ledger (lp:copy), charged as word ops: 0.83 / 0.88 / 0.91 ruint per copy. Copies per number: 303 / 488 / 994.

A re-price would follow only if the per-copy time tracks list length (a word-per-entry charge already does) or memory (outside an op count, like the sieve's memory cost; see the op-class draft's exclusions).

## Meter-health check (I-042) built and run (overnight stage 4; report only; never feeds fitness; INFORMATION ONLY, no sealed predictions)

**Tool:** `evolve/meterhealth.py` (e2079b0). It takes regions from the wall replicates and sub-regions (LPBREAK lp:*, SIEVEBREAK sv:*) from one breakdown pass per cell.
- **(a) Absolute:** each region's wall against its ruint priced at the cell's own mean rate (cell wall / cell ruint). Flag when the excess is more than **K = 3 × the region's own noise** (its sd over replicates; for a sub-region, the parent's sd scaled by its share of the parent's time) **and more than 1 µs per number.**
  - A flag means "slower per ruint than the cell's mean", **not necessarily an uncharged op.**
  - scan's ops are priced in the sieve region, so scan alone is never flagged; combined rows sieve+scan and sv:zero+scan carry that comparison.
- **(b) Differential:** for a pair (gene toggle), each region's change in wall against its change in ruint priced at the base region's own rate. Flag when the excess is **> 10 µs per number and > 5% of the base region's wall** (and the 95% interval excludes zero, where replicates exist).
- The sieve sub-regions are priced by their op units (sv:zero and sv:free2 as sieve_scan, sv:prime and sv:power as sieve_update and word); sv:tail keeps the rest.

**Test on existing outputs (no new timing; `evolve/meterhealth_existing.out`):**
- **It flags sv:free2 on the uncorrected 2b-sizes data** (2′b+pp3 +0, 96): (a) +39.7 µs against noise 0.9, and (b) +39.7 µs as a new cost. That was the test's requirement.
- **Also flagged:**
  - (b) the sieve against 2′b, +52.5 µs [+44.3, +60.5] (2b-sizes) and +58 to +68 µs (run A, pp cells);
  - (b) lp_ledger +32.4 µs (2b-sizes);
  - (a) lp:copy (+73 to +112 µs at 96) and lp:hash (+34 to +108 µs) in every cell.

**One timed pass (information only; `evolve/meterhealth_run.out`, `meterhealth_run.json`):**
- **Cells:** 2′a and 2′b at 72, 84 and 96; 4 replicates; flags off for the wall replicates; one pass per cell with both breakdowns on.
- **Machine:** AC online, cap 2,400 MHz on all cores, TCPU 52 °C before and 55 °C after, no Wolfram kernels, core 2's median 2,400 MHz in every cell (10–55 samples per pass). Load 2.5–3.2: a background agent (the scorecard tally) and Chrome were active; core 2 was pinned.
- **Wall (µs per number):** 72: 2′a 788.6, 2′b 708.6. 84: 2′a 1,644.3, 2′b 1,433.4. 96: 2′a 3,754.1, 2′b 3,328.7. Within ~1% of 2b-sizes and run A. **Information, not a verdict.**
- **(b) 2′b against 2′a: no flags at any size.** Every region's wall change tracks its price change. Confirm's wall falls slightly more than its price (excess −5.3 / −7.0 / −11.9 µs); setup at 96 +3.9 µs [+1.5, +6.3]; the sieve at 96 +9.6 [−3.2, +22.5]. **Root confirm carries no uncharged work by this check.**
- **(a) Flags common to both cells** (relation-identical, so they cancel in (b)):
  - setup (+53 to +96 µs);
  - solve (+18 / +73 / +176 µs at 72 / 84 / 96);
  - lp_ledger (+17 / +57–61 / +244 µs), within it lp:copy (+5 / +100 µs at 84 / 96) and lp:hash (+8 / +16 / +72–78 µs);
  - gray (+7 / +27 µs at 84 / 96).

## W3: cross-run drift of wall ratios (model, not a verdict; information only; `wolfram/2026-10-27_w3_drift.wl`, `.out`)

**What it computed.** Per-replicate paired wall ratios (cell / base, same replicate) from every capped timed run since i032-2prime: i032-2prime, pp3-gap-and-shift, shift-past-2, shift-72-84, 2b-sizes, and the overnight meter-health pass (information only, 4 replicates). All runs are capped at 2,400 MHz on AC and use the same `S2.map_nums` numbers per size. Seven cell pairs were timed in two or more runs: 2′b / 2′a at 72, 84 and 96 (96 in three runs); and at 96, 2′b+pp3 +0 / 2′a, +0 / 2′b, +1 / 2′a and +2 / 2′a. The model is random effects: each run's mean ratio = the pair's true ratio + a run effect (sd τ, shared across pairs) + within-run error (its own s.e.).

**Results (points = 100 × ratio):**

| set | df | Cochran Q (p) | τ, DL | τ, 95% Q-profile | cross-run difference, 95% half-width (DL / τ at upper bound) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all seven pairs | 8 | 10.06 (0.26) | 0.20 | [0, 0.94] | ±1.30 / ±2.87 |
| without 96 +0 / 2′b | 7 | 7.76 (0.35) | 0.12 | [0, 0.82] | ±1.11 / ±2.50 |
| 2′b / 2′a only | 4 | 2.44 (0.66) | 0.00 | [0, 0.60] | ±0.88 / ±1.89 |

- **Within-run s.e. of a run's mean ratio:** 0.25–0.78 points (typical 0.38–0.42 for eight replicates).
- **The between-run run effect is not distinguishable from zero** on these data (Q p = 0.26). The ±1.5 seen between pp3-gap-and-shift and shift-past-2 for +2 (86.50 vs 88.01) is 2.2 times its own within-run s.e. of the difference (0.68): the largest of the seven, but the pooled spread is what within-run noise predicts.
- **2′b / 2′a repeats closely:** 90.38 / 89.85 at 72; 87.06 / 87.17 at 84; 88.39 / 88.77 / 88.67 at 96.
- **The 96 +0 / 2′b pair straddles the free-2 meter correction** (6031239): i032-2prime ran before it, 2b-sizes after. The correction adds a charge call per polynomial, so part of its 1.5-point gap (101.98 vs 103.51) may be real code change, not drift. Hence the second row.

**What it does not establish.** Seven pairs and nine degrees of freedom give a weak bound on τ: the Q-profile upper limit (0.94) is almost five times the point estimate. All runs are one machine on one day with one cap; it says nothing about other days, temperatures or machines. Clock options differ between runs (period, inner, skip_launch at 72 and 84), and are folded into τ.

**Recommendation (the user's to adopt; nothing changed):** keep **±1.5 points** in the PROTOCOL guard for comparisons between two 8-replicate runs: it sits above the point estimate (±1.1–1.3) and below the upper bound (±2.5–2.9). Where either run has 4 replicates, use ±2.0. Revisit when more pairs repeat.

## W4: forecaster calibration (tally, not a verdict; information only; `wolfram/2026-10-27_w4_calibration.wl`, `.out`; section 3a of `reviews/scorecard.md`)

**What it computed.**
- **Stated confidences:** Brier scores for the five scored predictions that state a confidence (DeepSeek: D-9, D-14; Grok: G-4, G-7, G-9; the reviewer states none). DeepSeek scores 0.336 and Grok 0.282 as scored; under the corrected meter 0.186 and 0.182 (0.25 = always 50%).
- **Sealed ranges:** width against hit rate for 110 sealed numeric ranges from the five card runs since i032-2prime. The reviewer hit 31 of 35 (89%, median z 0.50); DeepSeek 23 of 38 (61%, 0.55); Grok 24 of 37 (65%, 0.53). DeepSeek's and Grok's ratio ranges are narrower (1.8–2.0 points against the reviewer's 3.0), and their misses are far outside the range (upper-quartile z 1.6–2.3).
- **Reading:** DeepSeek and Grok are over-confident in range width, driven by tails. The reviewer is close to a ~90% interval.

**What it does not establish.** Five confidence rows cannot calibrate anything (1 hit in 5: 95% interval 4–62%). Ranges within a run share anchors, so they are not independent. The µs misses largely repeat one error (the "241 µs" anchor). The extraction was delegated and spot-checked on 8 rows. The new PROTOCOL prediction guards (arithmetic bands; transfers widened by drift) address the narrow-range pattern prospectively; nothing is re-scored here.

## W1: where root confirm would cross 1.000 on official (model, not a verdict; information only; `wolfram/2026-10-27_w1_crossover.wl`, `.out`)

**What it computed.** Fits of 2′b against 2′a priced ratios at 72 / 84 / 96 bits: official 1.0403 / 1.0242 / 1.0137; ruint 0.8896 / 0.8699 / 0.8877; Montgomery 0.8820 / 0.8638 / 0.8838. The 72/84 ratios come from 2b-sizes and the 96 ratio from i032-2prime; the free-2 correction does not touch either cell. The fits are against bits and against log F. F, the mean factor-base size over all map numbers, is 57.5 / 95.3 / 139.8, from Python traces of the reference genes with goff = 1 (no timing, no priced totals; 96 matches card_params' 138).

**Official, where it reaches 1.000:**

| shape | crossing | 95% range | residual df |
|---|---|---|---|
| straight line in bits | **107.5 bits** | from 90 bits; the band's upper edge never reaches 1.000 | 1 (t = 12.7) |
| straight line in log F | F ≈ 218, **≈ 107 bits** | 98–134 bits (F→bits by the fitted log F–bits line, itself an extrapolation) | 1 |
| exponential decay to 0 in bits | never (official stays above 1.000) | | 1 |
| power law in F | never (e ∝ F^−1.14) | | 1 |
| exact 3-point exponential with offset | 128.6 bits | | 0 |
| exact quadratic in bits | never (minimum excess +0.8% at 113 bits) | | 0 |

- **Official's excess shrinks more slowly with size:** it falls 1.61 points from 72 to 84 and 1.06 from 84 to 96 (ratio 0.66). Straight lines ignore that slowdown, and the curved shapes that follow it level off above 1.000 or cross only past 128 bits.
- **ruint and Montgomery show no trend:** slopes −0.00008 and +0.00008 per bit, R² < 0.01. Both stay at 0.86–0.89, with 84 lowest at both.

**How weak this is.** With three points, a line keeps one residual degree of freedom, so its 95% band uses t = 12.7, and any three-parameter curve fits them exactly. The data cannot pick a shape, and the forecasts span **107 bits to never**. The straight-line 107 bits is the optimistic end, not a central estimate. Measuring official at 108 or 120 bits, a count pass with no timing, would separate the shapes. Both sizes are above the project's 40–100-bit scope, so that is the user's call.

**What it does not establish.** This is a model, not a verdict. It says nothing about the robust-rule decision, and it computes no op-class figure.

## W2: kept-relation copies, growth with size (model, not a verdict; information only; `wolfram/2026-10-27_w2_copies.wl`, `.out`)

**What it computed.** The copies' (lp:copy) wall excess over price for 2′a at 72 / 84 / 96 bits, from the overnight meter-health pass. Each factor (copies per number, ns per copy, ruint per copy, the cell's rate, total wall) is extrapolated log-linearly in bits. lp:copy's wall agrees with the shift runs' breakdowns to within 1–5 µs.

| bits | copies / number | ns / copy | wall ÷ price | excess µs / number | excess share of wall | copies' whole share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 72 | 303 | 43 | 0.57 | −9.7 | −1.2% | 1.6% |
| 84 | 489 | 76 | 1.18 | +5.7 | +0.3% | 2.3% |
| 96 | 994 | 158 | 2.71 | +99.3 | +2.65% | 4.2% |

- **This pass gives 2.71× and +99.3 µs at 96;** stage 5's 2.59× and +93.9 µs came from a different cell and run. The per-copy time grows ×1.93 per 12 bits, faster than the list length (ns per copy ∝ F^1.46), which points at memory (allocation and cold cache) rather than the words copied. The price per copy grows only ×1.05 per 12 bits.

**Forecast, as a share of total wall:**

| bits | model A (ns per copy keeps growing) | model B (ns per copy stays at 96's 158 ns) |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | +159 µs, 3.3% | +120 µs, 2.5% |
| 108 | +427 µs, 5.3% | +185 µs, 2.3% |
| 116 | +1,066 µs, 7.9% | +286 µs, 2.1% |
| 128 | +3,953 µs, 13.3% | +543 µs, 1.8% |

**Urgency, as a model reading:**
- Inside the project's scope (≤ 100 bits), the copies' excess is 2.5–3.3% of wall: real, but about the size of the ±1.5-point cross-run drift. It does not move a within-run verdict on its own.
- It matters before any scale-up past ~100 bits only if per-copy time keeps growing (model A). Model B, where per-copy time stops growing, keeps it near 2%.
- The data cannot tell A from B: the 95% band on ns per copy at 128 bits is 111–7,118 ns. What would separate them is a microbenchmark of one copy at the list lengths of 108 and 120 bits, the measurement stage 5 already proposed.

**What it does not establish.** Each fit rests on three points with one residual degree of freedom, from one information-only pass on one machine. The breakdown's sub-timer overhead sits inside lp:copy's wall and was not measured separately, and that overhead may be part of the "excess". Sizes above 100 bits are outside the project's scope. No re-price is implied; that is the user's decision, after the measurement.

## W5 (reduced): light-meter per-number check (model, not a verdict; information only; `wolfram/2026-10-27_w5_lightmeter.wl`, `.out`)

**The I-033 decile curve was not possible from repo inputs.** Stage F (`evolve/stagef.json`, 352cfa8) ran the yield model on only 8 map numbers per size, and only at 84 and 96: there is no 72. The measured true fulls and partials (`step9.json`) are pooled per size, not kept per number. Deciles need per-number measured yield on many more numbers; that would be a new trace run, not done.

**What was checked instead.** The quantities stage F does keep per number: polynomials to completion and combinations, model (given stage B's pooled capture) against the card.

| | 84 bits | 96 bits |
|---|---|---|
| single factor k (card = k × model) | 1.008 | 1.065 |
| per-number scatter, before / after the factor | 13.6% / 13.7% | 15.7% / 16.7% |
| slope of log card on log model (95%) | 0.75 (0.46–1.05) | 1.28 (0.91–1.65) |
| ranking, Spearman ρ (polynomials) | 0.79 | 0.93 |
| ranking, Spearman ρ (combinations) | 0.48 | 0.56 |

- **One factor fixes the mean but not the scatter:** after it, single numbers are still off by 14–17%.
- **The slopes point opposite ways at the two sizes:** at 84, the model's misses are largest on the hardest numbers; at 96, on the easiest. Both intervals include 1. Eight numbers cannot tell a yield-dependent error from noise.
- **Ranking is good on polynomials** (ρ 0.79 and 0.93) and weak on combinations (0.48 and 0.56).

**For I-024 (per-number budgets):** the model ranks numbers by difficulty well enough to sort them, but a single number's polynomial count is uncertain to about ±15%. Whether the error depends on yield is open.

**What it does not establish.** This is not I-033's curve: 8 numbers per size, no 72. Capture is stage B's pooled rate applied to every number, so per-number capture differences show up as model error. The full curve needs per-number traces (true fulls and partials) on a few hundred map numbers at 72, 84 and 96. That is a trace run, read-only for the card; the user decides whether to run it (I-033 decision pending).

## op-class v1, step 2: counts and frozen weights (no priced figure; step 3 not authorised)

**Order kept:**
- **Step 2.1 (1035971), before any count:** the toolchain, the binary hashes, the code identity of the debug build against release, the line map and the input set were committed.
- **Step 2.2:** two separate agents each derived the weights. Each was given only the procedure, the map, the input set and the binaries, and wrote its own attribution code. Neither saw any priced figure or the other's work.
- **Step 2.3:** the comparison and the static cross-check.
- **Step 2.4 (df5a0e3):** the weights frozen as "op-class v1" (`opclass/opclass_v1.json`).

**Agreement:** A and B agree within **5.7 × 10⁻⁵ per class** (the tolerance is 2%; the largest difference is hash, then cfrac_ops at 3 × 10⁻⁷; `opclass/compare.out`). Both pass the sum check in every run: classes + meter + uncharged + decl + unattributed = callgrind's total, within 4 × 10⁻⁶ Ir. Total: 138.22 × 10⁹ Ir over 17 runs.
- **Where the total goes:** meter 3.17%, uncharged:card 7.97%, uncharged:harness 0.19%, unattributed 0.005%, decl 0.0007%.

**Weights (Ir per charged op; fraction against root_test):**

| class | weight | fraction | | class | weight | fraction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| setup_gray | 4.87 | 0.093 | | lp_small | 68.2 | 1.305 |
| f64_div | 6.00 | 0.115 | | confirm_td | 108.5 | 2.074 |
| sieve_update | 11.09 | 0.212 | | cfrac_ops (lump) | 110.1 | 2.105 |
| sieve_scan | 14.89 | 0.285 | | setup_euclid_N | 112.6 | 2.154 |
| fb | 27.2 | 0.521 | | f64_log | 135.9 | 2.599 |
| la | 28.4 | 0.543 | | sqrt_gcd | 159.7 | 3.054 |
| td_mod | 29.0 | 0.555 | | setup_small | 178.8 | 3.419 |
| setup_euclid | 39.4 | 0.753 | | sqrt_mul | 299.5 | 5.727 |
| root_test | 52.3 | 1 | | setup_mul | 306.4 | 5.859 |
| word | 55.6 | 1.063 | | check | 337.1 | 6.447 |
| mult | 64.0 | 1.225 | | hash | 465.4 | 8.901 |
| sort_cmp | 67.4 | 1.289 | | mul | 554.9 | 10.611 |
| ps_ops (lump) | 0.283 | 0.005 | | lp_full | 649.4 | 12.419 |
| | | | | sq_ops (lump) | 1,266 | 24.22 |
| | | | | gcd | 1,402 | 26.81 |

setup_full and confirm_full are charged by no card and get no weight.

**Resolved in writing (no re-tuning toward any outcome):**
1. **Line-0 rows** (DWARF line 0 in every lampcore frame; mostly in `qs::sieve_source`; about 2.5 × 10⁹ Ir). Both derivations, independently, read R2/R3 literally: a line-0 frame has no line, so the instruction moves outward, and by R3 to the caller's line (qs.rs 237, uncharged:card). **Kept as the v1 reading.** The rules were committed before counting, and the alternative was raised only after the weights were seen.
   - The alternative, the nearest preceding instruction's line, would raise root_test by about 4%, la by 4–11%, lp_small by 12%, and confirm_td and setup_euclid by about 5%. It also gives A and B results 6.7% apart, so as written it is under-specified.
   - Recorded as a known limitation: line-0 code inside charged loops is counted as uncharged:card in v1.
2. **Ir in runs with no ops of the class** (R6 pools over all runs): check gets 7.6M Ir from the gene tests on qs.rs 376–379, evaluated when the check is off. That makes its weight 337.1 pooled, against 272.9 from C_check alone. root_test gets 3.9M Ir in the 2′a runs, from its branch tests; cfrac_ops gets 46k.
   - **Kept as R6 says.** The source is the map: those lines are tests that run whatever the gene's value. It is noted for a v2 map.
3. **Decl lines:** main.rs 385 and qs.rs 394 got 0.9M Ir (0.0007%), from code DWARF puts on a brace and a doc line. Reported, not reassigned.

**Stability:**
- **Single-run classes,** with no cross-run spread to measure: check, setup_mul (1,870 ops), setup_euclid_N (2,775), td_mod, sq_ops, ps_ops, cfrac_ops.
  - setup_mul and setup_euclid_N are the "too few ops" classes. Instruction counts are deterministic, so their weights are exact for the committed mix, but that mix is one ECM run on 96 numbers.
  - **Kept, flagged for the user.**
- **Spread across runs above 2%** in most multi-run classes, from the mix, not from noise: the same type covers different work in different lamps and sizes.
  - word: 1.3 in p−1 stage 2 against 38–71 in qs;
  - gcd: rho, p−1 and ecm;
  - mult: 36.6 at 54 bits against 65.7 elsewhere;
  - confirm_td: 106–110 in full-pass runs, 136–140 in 2′b runs.
  - root_test (0.6%) and f64_div (0%) are within 2%.
  - **A v1 weight is an average over the committed input mix, and is valid for that mix.**

**Static cross-check** (`opclass/static_crosscheck.md`): root_test is within 10% (54 static against 52.3). The others that differ by more than 10% are explained:
- sieve_update +11%: the per-root work around the walk;
- sieve_scan: glibc `memset`'s `rep stosb`, which callgrind counts per repetition (about 4 per cell; with it, 15 against 14.9);
- setup_gray: only the d > 0 branch is vectorised (2.6 against about 7.5 per root; mean about 5.0, against 4.87);
- la: the charge is a formula, not the XORs done;
- setup_euclid: a fixed cost per inverse spread over a few steps.

The library-bound classes have no single static body and are dynamic only.

**Lumps** (IDEAS I-043, typing them is a meter change): cfrac_ops 110.1, sq_ops 1,266 and ps_ops 0.283 Ir per op, each an average over its supplementary run. ps is a replay that charges FFT-model ops without doing the arithmetic, so its weight does not measure the charged work.

**What this does not establish:** no pricing has been applied. No break-even, no op-class ratio for any cell and no robust ratio under option (b) have been computed; that is step 3, the user's word. Memory cost is excluded (procedure, section 5): instruction counts are fixed by the binary, not by clock speed.

| bits | op-class | ruint | Montgomery | **robust (b)** | (e) | official (no veto) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Adopted: root confirm (2′b), Oct 27 (the user's decision)

- **The new reference genes:** goff = 1 (already the reference since Oct 26) and **confirm = root**, i.e. the sealed genes with kset sf32 (`lctest.ref(bits)`) plus `goff=1, confirm="root"`.
  - As with 2′a, runners pass the genes explicitly. `lctest.ref()` and the gene's code default (confirm off) are unchanged, so every earlier script reproduces as committed.
  - Making them the code default would change what earlier scripts compute on a rerun. It can be a separate commit if the user wants it.

### DeepSeek on step 3 (received 07:49 Oct 27 PT; information only; verbatim)

<!-- verbatim begin -->
## Recorded

- The "worst of four can never lower a worst" flaw is accepted: adding an op-class pricing alongside official could never change an adoption, because the minimum over a larger set can only rise. My round-59 proposal had the same defect. **Option (b), op-class replacing official in the robust track with official reported but not vetoing, is recorded as the user's choice, committed before any count.**
- Procedure adopted as described: whole-run callgrind Ir over a committed input set, committed source-line→op-class map covering every charged line, divided by the meter's per-type counts; no hand-picked sequences; two independent derivations agreeing to 0.006%. Weights **op-class v1** frozen; known issues (line-0 ~2.5e9 instructions, pooled word weight 1.3–71 across lamps, "check" inflation) recorded before any ratio. Any v2 is prospective only.
- Step 3 results recorded: 2'b vs 2'a op-class 0.8657 / 0.8293 / 0.8436 at 72/84/96, robust (ruint) 0.8896 / 0.8699 / 0.8877, **better at every size**, intervals excluding 1. Official reported but not vetoing: 1.0403 / 1.0242 / 1.0137. Reviewer's correction accepted: official's veto on 2'b was **not** about sieve updates; it charges a root test like a 128-bit trial division, and a root test is about half (52.3 vs 108.5 instructions).

## 1. Strongest remaining reason not to adopt 2'b now, and the check I want first

**The strongest reason is that op-class v1 has never been shown to track wall time per op class on this machine, and the deciding quantity is exactly the root-test weight.** The break-even is 1.71–1.87× v1, i.e. 89–98 instructions against 52.3; but we already have measured costs of roughly **0.70 ns per word op, 1.59 ns per prime for the branch-free root test, and 3.9 ns per prime divided for trial division**, so a root test costs about **2.4× more per instruction** than a word op and trial division about 2.8×. Instruction weights are therefore **not** wall-proportional, and whether that biases the comparison depends on the op mix; if a wall-proportional re-weighting moves the root-test weight toward the break-even, the 1.7–1.9× margin is overstated.

**Check I want first:** recompute the op-class ratio at 96 bits using **measured ns/op per class on a capped clock** and the actual per-type counts for 2'a and 2'b, and confirm it still clears 1.0 with the same margin. The microbenchmark that produced 1.59 ns was run on a throttled core (400 MHz before, 1,772 MHz after), so the ns/op figures themselves need a steady-clock repeat before they can arbitrate. If the wall-proportional ratio clears 1.0 by the same margin, adoption is on both an instruction and a time footing; if it does not, the adoption is resting on instruction counts rather than on time, and that should be said in the adoption record.

## 2. A future change op-class could wave through that official would rightly block

**The kind of change op-class is structurally unable to veto is one that replaces a charged op with instruction-cheap but latency- or memory-expensive work — a branch chain or lookup table in place of a division, or work moved into library calls and un-attributed lines.** Official's crude unit-cost rule is at least **implementation-blind**: it charges every declared op and so vetoes added work regardless of how clever the code is, whereas op-class's weights are instruction counts taken from **the card's own binary and source map**, and that map already leaves **~2.5×10⁹ instructions unattributed**. A change that trades divisions for branches, or mapped ops for `memcpy`/`malloc` copies like the kept-relation path already measured at **2.6× its price and +94 µs/number at 96 bits**, would read as a win on op-class while losing on wall time; the same hole would cover hash-table growth and any resizing or allocation the line map does not reach.
<!-- verbatim end -->

**The reviewer's notes:**
- **Q1 is already answered**, two ways:
  - by ruint, which is machine-time calibrated, is in the robust track, and is the pricing that set the robust ratio;
  - by measured wall-clock: −9.6% / −12.9% / −11.2%.

  DeepSeek's own ns figures make a root test 0.41 of a trial division, against v1's 0.48: that favours 2′b more.
- **Q2 accepted:** op-class is blind to latency and memory, and to unattributed code.

## Stage 2: external baseline, msieve 1.53 (I-038; information only, never fitness; `evolve/baseline_msieve.py`, `.out`, `.json`; predictions `predictions/baseline-msieve.md`, filed before timing)

**In plain English first: sieve against sieve, the balanced band (both factors half of N), our card is about 4–5 times faster than msieve as shipped:**

| bits | card (2′b) µs per number | msieve µs per number | **card / msieve, balanced band** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 72 | 883 | 4,764 | **0.185** [0.179, 0.192] |
| 84 | 1,591 | 6,213 | **0.256** [0.252, 0.260] |
| 96 | 3,570 | 17,005 | **0.210** [0.207, 0.213] |

**Why, and the main caveat.** At 29 digits msieve runs its generic QS (`evolve/baseline_msieve_96bal_example.log`, one balanced 96-bit number):
- a sieve interval of 4 × 32 KB blocks (our card: 2,109 positions);
- 270 factor-base primes;
- 713 relations collected where 366 are needed;
- every relation written to `msieve.dat` (about 100 KB per number) and read back for filtering.

msieve's small-number path is not tuned for 29-digit inputs. This compares the card against **msieve as shipped**, not against the best possible small-number SIQS. Its 17 ms per 96-bit number matches the usual msieve heuristic, exp(0.22 n − 10.7) s ≈ 13 ms at 29 digits, so it was not mis-run.

**Conditions:**
- AC online; the cap 2,400 MHz on every core; core 2 at a median of 2,400 MHz in every cell; no Wolfram kernel; TCPU below 70 °C at the start.
- Both tools in batch (one process per file), pinned to core 2, 4 replicates in a rotating order.
- **Factors identical on every number:** msieve's prime factors equal {p, q}, and the card's and the pipeline's factor is p or q, with 0 failures at every size.

**The sealed comparison** (the qs card, 2′b, against msieve; all map numbers; as filed):

| bits | card µs | msieve µs | **card / msieve** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 72 | 846 | 2,833 | **0.299** [0.294, 0.303] |
| 84 | 1,594 | 4,089 | **0.390** [0.385, 0.395] |
| 96 | 3,540 | 11,096 | **0.319** [0.310, 0.328] |

**Scored as filed:**
- **The reviewer's 96 claim** (0.7–6, central 2: msieve faster, by less than 10×; 65%): **missed.** 0.319 is below the range: the card is faster.
- **The reviewer's 72 claim** (closer to 1 than at 96; 60%): **missed.** |0.299 − 1| = 0.701 against |0.319 − 1| = 0.681; the intervals do not overlap.
- **D-18** (0.35–1.05, central 0.60; falsified if > 1.15 or < 0.20): **missed**, below the range. Not falsified (0.319 > 0.20).
- **D-19** (yes, 72 closer to 1; 75%): **falsified.** Its falsifier, |r72 − 1| ≥ |r96 − 1|, holds.
- **G-11** (0.6–2.5; 60%): **falsified.** Its falsifier is a ratio outside 0.6–2.5.
- **G-12** (yes, 72 closer to 1; 55%): **falsified.** Its falsifier, |r72 − 1| ≥ |r96 − 1|, holds.

**Reading the scores.** All three forecasters had msieve faster or level. The reviewer's annotation on D-18, computed from the heuristic D-18 rejected, gave about 0.26: the closest figure on file, though not a sealed prediction. The ordering questions failed narrowly but cleanly: the 72-bit ratio sits slightly further from 1 than the 96-bit one, because msieve's per-number cost at 72 bits is already dominated by its fixed QS set-up.

**Information cells** (same conditions and replicates):
- **The full reference pipeline** (td, rho, p−1, ecm, then the 2′b qs) against msieve, all map numbers: 0.260 [0.254, 0.267] / 0.346 [0.339, 0.352] / 0.265 [0.258, 0.272]. The pipeline is 13–17% faster than the qs card alone, because it takes the small factors cheaply.
- **Per band** (one pass each): msieve is faster where the smaller factor is 16–20 bits; it finds those by trial division or rho in under a millisecond. The ratio there is 2.2–3.8 (card slower), since the qs card runs full SIQS on every number. From 24 bits up the card is faster: 0.44–0.77 at 24 bits, about 0.2–0.28 above.
- **The build difference:** msieve's Makefile builds `-O3 -march=native`; lampcore is the baseline x86-64 target. msieve rebuilt `-march=x86-64` (`~/opt/msieve-src/msieve-1.53-x86-64`, sha256 2a9fc91d…) is 1.21× / 1.16× / 1.05× slower than native at 72 / 84 / 96 (one replicate). So the native build favours msieve, and like for like the card's lead would be slightly larger.

**Builds:** msieve 1.53 source tarball sha256 c5fcbaaf…4d93bb4 (Nov 2016). Native binary sha256 437f5da3…7d10eb, `make all NO_ZLIB=1`, no sudo; GMP from the system.

**Not established:** a comparison with a small-number-tuned SIQS (e.g. YAFU's tiny-SIQS path). Energy was not measured. One machine.

## Stage 3: kept-relation copies, cost note only (no code or meter change; the change is the user's decision)

**Finding: the cost that grows with size is not the copy. It is the A-prime index lookup next to it.** For every kept relation, the card finds each of A's s = 4 primes in the factor base with `pos` (qs.rs 607, used at 1238), a **linear scan** of the base.
- The A-primes sit at mean base index 21.6 / 38.7 / 79.5 at 72 / 84 / 96 (estimated 2 + π(p)/2, from traces), so a kept relation scans about 87 / 155 / 318 entries: in proportion 1 : 1.8 : 3.7.
- That is the same proportion as the per-call times measured in the lp:copy region: 43 : 76 : 158 ns (W2, stage 4b). The list copied is about the same length at every size: 10.8 / 11.5 / 11.7 entries.
- The meter charges these lookups only as the A-prime adds: 4 word per relation, flat, while the scan behind them grows with the A-primes' position in the base.

**Microbenchmark** (`bench/copybench`, a standalone crate mirroring lampcore's path, lampcore untouched; `evolve/copybench_run.py`, `.out`, `.json`):
- Conditions: capped 2,400 MHz, AC, pinned core 2, 5 replicates, medians.
- Inputs: from traces of the reference; 100–128 bits are model inputs.

| bits | kept / number | A-prime lookups, ns per kept relation | copy alone, ns |
|---|---|---|---|
| 72 | 296 | 46.6 | 22.9 |
| 84 | 462 | 81.8 | 22.4 |
| 96 | 927 | 165.1 | 51.9 |
| 100 (model) | 1,075 | 185 | 88 |
| 108 (model) | 1,573 | 246 | 78 |
| 116 (model) | 2,302 | 339 | 86 |
| 128 (model) | 4,073 | 568 | 70 |

- **The lookups alone reproduce the measured lp:copy times** (46.6 / 81.8 / 165 against 43 / 76 / 158 ns).
- **The copy is 22–52 ns,** larger at 96 as the arena outgrows the cache.
- **The "under sieve-sweep pressure" column** in the `.out` is information only: subtracting separately timed passes does not isolate the copy reliably.
- **The 128-bit model** puts the A-prime index past F; the benchmark clamps it. This is an extrapolation artefact.

**Proposals** (the Wolfram forecast: `wolfram/2026-10-27_copies_cost.wl`, `.out`; model, not a verdict):
1. **Recommended: a counts-identical code fix, not a re-price.** Look up the A-primes' base indices once per A, instead of a linear scan per kept relation. 2′b already computes them (`aj`); 2′a can do the same.
   - **No op count changes,** so no priced figure moves.
   - **Wall saved:** 13.8 / 37.8 / 153 µs per number, 1.6% / 2.4% / 4.3% of the reference's wall at 72 / 84 / 96 (model: 4.2–7.8% at 100–128).
   - 2′a and 2′b gain alike, so 2′b/2′a moves by under 0.1 point.
   - **It is a "counts-identical code change"** (PROTOCOL): a cost note before code, then acceptance (identical per number and per type, Python = Rust), then parity.
2. **The alternative: a meter change** that keeps the code and charges the scan, one word per base entry compared: + 26,758 / 73,366 / 298,494 word per number.
   - It raises both cells by 8–15% under ruint and Montgomery and by 17–21% under official, for work that is 1.6–4.3% of the wall, so it would **overprice under every pricing**.
   - Under op-class v1 the overpricing is about 30×: v1's word weight is an average over heterogeneous sites (known issue 2).
   - 2′b/2′a would move up: ruint 0.8877 → 0.9008 at 96, still better.
   - **Not recommended.**

**Not established:**
- The benchmark is a model of the card's path (synthetic primes, the same scan and copy code), not the card itself.
- The A-prime index is estimated from π(p).
- The 100–128 rows extrapolate three sizes.

## Cost note (before code): the A-prime lookup fix (the user's decision, Oct 27: YES)

**The change:** lampcore's `sieve_source` finds each A-prime's factor-base index with `pos` (qs.rs 607), a linear scan of the base, once per A in the setup (785) and, for 2′b, in `aj` (776), and **once per A-prime per kept relation** (1238). The fix computes the s indices **once per A**, in A's own order (`qj`), and the kept-relation loop reads `qj` instead of calling `pos`. The setup and `aj` read the same `qj`.
- **Python:** `qs.py` already looks indices up in a dict (`idx[ql]`, 575), O(1); no linear scan exists there. The Python loop is changed only to read the same per-A list, so both cores have the same shape. No Python op or count changes.

**Cost model:**
- **Charged ops: none change.** `pos` was never charged (the meter charges the A-prime adds as 4 word per relation, item 15, and keeps charging them exactly so). Every op count per type, per number, is predicted **identical**; every relation, its exponent vector and its order are predicted identical (the same indices, in the same order, enter `tt`).
- **Uncharged work removed:** about 87 / 155 / 318 base-entry compares per kept relation at 72 / 84 / 96 (Stage 3), replaced by s = 4 compares-and-scans per A (one scan per A-prime, as now in the setup).
- **No priced figure moves** (official, ruint, Montgomery, op-class v1: all are counts × weights). op-class v1 is frozen; the removed instructions were mostly the scan's, attributed to `pos`'s line (@caller → lp:copy's word): v1's weights are not re-derived (a v2 would be prospective).
- **Wall forecast** (Stage 3 model, `wolfram/2026-10-27_copies_cost`): −13.8 / −37.8 / −153 µs per number, i.e. 2′b+fix / 2′b ≈ 0.984 / 0.976 / 0.957 at 72 / 84 / 96. This is a model; the verdict will come from the sealed timing run (predictions filed first).

**Procedure:** code in lampcore and qs.py; acceptance (every count per type and every relation identical, 2′a and 2′b, Python = Rust, at 72 / 84 / 96); full parity; then the sealed timing run 2′b against 2′b+fix (predictions filed first; STOP at the prediction point).
